findings.issue_text: [BUG] Destructured mainHostDestinationCalendar is dereferenced without optional chaining, crashing when evt.destinationCalendar is null or empty. const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []; followed by mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration') whenever a Google Meet booking has no destination calendar (e.g. dynamic/round-robin paths where destinationCalendar is null), turning the Meet fallback into a 500 on booking creation.

[BUG] updateEvent's fallback branch compares cal.externalId === externalCalendarId inside the branch where externalCalendarId is falsy, so the find never matches and selectedCalendar is always undefined. When a booking reference has no externalCalendarId, the previous code fell back to event.destinationCalendar?.externalId; now every Google event update on such a booking sends calendarId: undefined to the Google API and fails, breaking reschedule/location-edit of pre-refactor bookings.

[BUG] deleteEvent has the same inverted-guard bug: the fallback searches for a destination calendar whose externalId equals an externalCalendarId that is falsy in that branch, so calendarId is always undefined when externalCalendarId is absent. Cancelling a booking whose reference lacks externalCalendarId (pre-refactor bookings and the non-credentialId create path, which now stores no externalId) passes calendarId: undefined to calendar.events.delete, leaving orphaned events on the host's Google calendar.

[BUG] The new externalId parameter is accepted and echoed into the EventResult but never passed to calendar.createEvent, and the non-credentialId call sites in EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents invoke createEvent without it, so result.externalId is undefined on that path. EventManager then stores externalCalendarId: undefined in the booking reference for every credential-less destination calendar; combined with the Google fallback bugs above, every subsequent update/delete of those events targets an undefined calendar and fails.

[BUG] evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars) is a silent no-op when evt.destinationCalendar was set to null two lines earlier, dropping all team-host destination calendars for collective bookings whose organizer has no destination calendar. For a COLLECTIVE event type with no eventType-level destinationCalendar and an organizer without one, team members' calendars are silently discarded and events are created on none of the team hosts' calendars — the exact collective-multi-host case this PR claims to fix.

[ADVISORY] The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId) but only the Google implementation was updated; every other Calendar implementation in the repo (BaseCalendarService subclasses, other app-store calendars) still implements the one-parameter signature and ignores credentialId. Any future caller relying on the interface contract to select a per-credential destination calendar gets silent no-op behavior from every non-Google provider; TypeScript method bivariance hides this today, so nothing flags the drift at compile time. The next person touching createEvent gets harder-to-trace behavior across providers.

[BUG] Destructuring `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` followed by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` throws a TypeError when destinationCalendar is null or empty. For any booking where neither eventType nor organizer has a destinationCalendar (handleNewBooking.ts sets destinationCalendar: null in exactly that case), `?? []` yields an empty array, destructuring gives undefined, and `undefined.integration` throws — EventManager.create crashes and the entire booking creation fails with a 500, whereas the old code `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` safely fell through to the Cal Video fallback.

[BUG] In updateEvent the fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` can never match because it only executes when externalCalendarId is falsy, so the find predicate compares against null/undefined and always returns undefined. When EventManager.update calls updateEvent with a null externalCalendarId (calendarReference found without externalCalendarId), selectedCalendar is undefined, calendar.events.update is invoked with calendarId undefined, and Google returns 'Missing required query parameter calendarId' — reschedule updates that previously fell back to destinationCalendar.externalId now fail and the calendar event is silently left stale.

[BUG] deleteEvent has the same dead fallback: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is only reached when externalCalendarId is falsy, so the find never matches and calendarId is undefined. Deleting a booking whose calendar reference lacks externalCalendarId (or any code path passing null) makes calendar.events.delete call Google with calendarId undefined, which errors — the Google event is never deleted and stays on the host's calendar after the booking is cancelled.

[ADVISORY] The entire new collective multi-host destination calendar behavior (teamDestinationCalendars accumulation, the per-destination create loop with DB credential fallback in EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents, and Google's credentialId-based calendar selection) has no verification in this diff — the only test change is flipping a single e2e fixture from `destinationCalendar: null` to `destinationCalendar: []` in webhook.e2e.ts. A regression in the DB credential fetch (prisma.credential.findUnique path), the per-destination loop, or the empty-array crash mode found above would ship undetected; collective bookings with multiple Google hosts would silently create events on only one host's calendar, and nothing in CI would notice.

[ADVISORY] Only GoogleCalendarService was updated to select the destination calendar matching the passed credentialId; larkcalendar (and office365calendar) still destructure only the first destination calendar (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []`), so the multi-host feature silently no-ops for non-Google hosts. A collective event whose non-organizer hosts use Lark or Office 365 calendars gets written only to the first host's calendar even though the destinationCalendar array carries all hosts' entries — team members' calendars never receive the event and no error or warning is raised, leaving users with a partial multi-host implementation that differs by integration.

[BUG] The Google Meet fallback reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining, so it throws TypeError when destinationCalendar is null/empty. Bookings by users with no destinationCalendar and location=Google Meet crash with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading integration)' inside EventManager.create, aborting booking creation entirely.

[BUG] The updateEvent fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is executed only when externalCalendarId is falsy, so find never matches and the previous destinationCalendar fallback is destroyed. Updating a booking whose reference lacks externalCalendarId now passes calendarId=undefined to the Google API, failing with 404/400 instead of updating the event in the destination calendar as before.

[BUG] deleteEvent has the same dead fallback: inside the `externalCalendarId ? ... : find(cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` branch, externalCalendarId is falsy so find always returns undefined. Cancelling a booking whose calendar reference has no externalCalendarId silently fails to delete the Google event (calendarId=undefined), leaving orphaned events on users' calendars.

[BUG] In the reference.credentialId branch of the update loop, updateEvent(credential, ...) is called even when the credential is still undefined after the DB fallback fails. Unlike the create path which guards with `if (credential)`, update/reschedule of a booking whose referenced credential was deleted (DB lookup returns null) calls updateEvent(undefined, ...), which crashes inside getCalendar/CalendarManager with an unhandled TypeError.

[BUG] The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId: number), but only GoogleCalendarService was updated — LarkCalendarService, Office365CalendarService and BaseCalendarService still declare createEvent(event) with one parameter. Every non-Google calendar implementation now violates the interface (type errors at build), and any polymorphic call site passing credentialId hits an implementation that silently ignores it, defeating the credentialId-matching invariant this PR claims to establish.

[BUG] Google createEvent falls back to calendarId 'primary' when no destinationCalendar entry matches the credentialId, but CalendarManager/EventManager still record destination.externalId (or the passed externalId) as the booking reference's externalCalendarId. For a destinationCalendar whose credentialId doesn't match the credential used (e.g. team destination pointing at another host's credential), the event is created in 'primary' while the reference stores a different calendar id — later update/delete of that booking targets the wrong calendar and 404s.

[BUG] For COLLECTIVE team events, team hosts' destinationCalendars are appended via `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)`, which is a no-op when the organizer has no destinationCalendar (evt.destinationCalendar is null). The stated invariant of this PR — every collective host's destination calendar receives the event — silently fails whenever the organizer lacks a destinationCalendar: team hosts' calendars are dropped and events are only created via the default-credential fallback path.

[BUG] The rewritten loadUsers drops `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the non-eventType user query, removing the organization slug from every loaded user object. Any downstream consumer of the loaded users relying on user.organization.slug (e.g. org-aware routing/booking logic on dynamic collective links) now reads undefined and misroutes; the rewrite is also not traceable to the stated collective-destination-calendar intent.

[ADVISORY] The IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED spread inversion (`...(!X && {slug})` → `...(X ? {slug} : {})`) changes org-creation behavior and is entirely unrelated to the stated destinationCalendar fix. Operators/reviewers of this PR get a silent behavior change to organization slug handling (slug no longer stored when team billing is off, requestedSlug metadata semantics flipped) hidden inside a calendar PR; any regression there is unattributable to this change's intent.

[ADVISORY] Unrelated cosmetic rewrites ("organiser"→"organizer", reformatting of the catch block) and the orginalBookingDuration typo fix in handleNewBooking are bundled into this PR. Not traceable to any requirement in the stated intent; the diff noise increases review risk because behavior-adjacent lines were reformatted, making bisecting any calendar regression harder.

[ADVISORY] teamMemberPromises now always maps users.slice(1) and adds empty firstName/lastName fields, and the previous users.length>1 guard was dropped — a shape change to the attendees list not required by the collective-destinationCalendar intent. Email templates and downstream consumers of teamMembers receive new empty-string fields for every booking, and single-user bookings now build a (harmless but changed) promise pipeline; drift here is unreviewable against the stated intent and risks regressions in email rendering tests.

[BUG] updateEvent's fallback branch compares destinationCalendar entries against externalCalendarId inside a branch where externalCalendarId is falsy, so the find never matches and selectedCalendar is always undefined. Every Google update that reaches the fallback (externalCalendarId null/empty) previously used event.destinationCalendar.externalId; now it passes calendarId: undefined to calendar.events.update, so all such updates fail with a Google API error and reschedules/edits of bookings without a stored externalCalendarId break.

[BUG] deleteEvent repeats the same broken pattern: `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` — in the else branch externalCalendarId is falsy so the find predicate never matches. The old fallback to event.destinationCalendar.externalId is dead; calendarId becomes undefined and calendar.events.delete is called with calendarId: undefined, so cancellations of bookings lacking a stored externalCalendarId fail instead of deleting the event.

[BUG] The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId: number), but only GoogleCalendarService was updated — LarkCalendarService.createEvent(event), Office365CalendarService.createEvent(event), and BaseCalendarService still declare/accept a single-event signature. Every other Calendar implementer no longer satisfies the interface (compile failure in any typechecked consumer of Calendar), and CalendarManager.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id) passes a second argument these services silently ignore — the credentialId parameter reaches only Google, so any per-credential behavior indexed off it diverges by provider.

[BUG] CalendarManager.createEvent accepts destination.externalId as a parameter but never passes it to the calendar service; GoogleCalendarService selects the calendar by credentialId match and falls back to "primary", while CalendarManager unconditionally records the passed-in externalId as result.externalId. When the destinationCalendar entry's credentialId doesn't match the credential being used (e.g. shared/team destination calendars), the event is created on the Google account's "primary" calendar but the booking reference stores destination.externalId — subsequent updates/deletes target a calendar where the event was never created and fail with 404, the exact class of bug this PR claims to fix.

[BUG] The recurring-cancellation branch was moved inside the per-reference loop but ignores the loop's reference: for every calendar reference it re-runs `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...endsWith('_calendar'))` and deletes all updated bookings' events across all credentials. A booking with N calendar references now issues N × (all user calendar credentials) × updatedBookings deleteEvent calls for one logical cancel — duplicate deletions (extra external API calls, spurious 404/log errors) and N-fold fan-out on the reference-x-credential pattern.

[ADVISORY] `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently drops all team members' destination calendars when the organizer/eventType has no destinationCalendar (evt.destinationCalendar is null), because the optional chain skips the push. A COLLECTIVE team booking whose organizer has no personal destination calendar creates events on none of the team hosts' calendars even though each host configured one; the next editor will not see why hosts' calendars were skipped.

[ADVISORY] loadUsers dropped the `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` include from the non-eventTypeId query while keeping the rest of userSelect, removing organization data from the user objects on the dynamic-link path. Any downstream consumer of these users reading user.organization.slug (org routing, booking emails, team resolution) gets undefined for dynamic collective bookings; the change is unrelated to the PR's stated purpose so nothing flags it.

[ADVISORY] The update path changed `credentialId: result.credentialId ?? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId` to `credentialId: result.credentialId ?? undefined` while other places grew DB-fetch fallbacks for missing credentials. For legacy bookings whose updateEvent result lacks credentialId, the stored reference now persists credentialId: undefined where it previously recorded the destination calendar's credentialId — those references then fall into the slow 'iterate all user credentials' path on every later update/delete, compounding per-booking API fan-out.

[ADVISORY] The Google Meet fallback checks only the first destination calendar (`mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"`), so a multi-host collective event where a non-first host has the Google destination calendar silently downgrades location to integrations:daily. Collective bookings with mixed calendar integrations lose Google Meet links depending on array ordering — an ordering-dependent behavior change that no caller can reason about.

[ADVISORY] Google's createEvent destructures a `mainHostDestinationCalendar` (first element) for the organizer email but selects the target calendar by credentialId; the two selections can disagree, writing the event to calendar B while telling Google the organizer is calendar A's address. For multi-host events the organizer email sent in the payload can belong to a different calendar than the one the event is inserted into, producing Google-side organizer/attendee inconsistencies for exactly the collective case this PR targets.

[BUG] The refactor inverts the team-billing condition for the organization slug: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` became `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, so the slug is now written exactly when it previously was withheld, and withheld when it previously was written. When team billing is disabled (self-hosted installs), newly created organizations get no slug but get requestedSlug in metadata instead, and when billing is enabled they get a raw slug without the requestedSlug/verification flow — the organization-creation objective (slug gated behind billing/verification) is silently reversed for every user.

[BUG] `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` dereferences a destructured element that is undefined whenever `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or empty (the `?? []` fallback guarantees it), throwing `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')`. Any Google-Meet-location booking with no destination calendar (previously handled: `undefined !== "google_calendar"` was true) crashes EventManager.createAllEvents instead of falling back to Cal Video — the accepted 'fallback to integrations:daily' intent is replaced by a hard failure.

[BUG] The `updateEvent` fallback branch computes `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` inside a branch where `externalCalendarId` is falsy (null/empty), so the find predicate can never match and the expression is always undefined. Updating a legacy booking whose calendar reference has no externalCalendarId now passes `calendarId: undefined` to the Google API instead of the destination calendar's externalId, failing every reschedule/edit for bookings whose reference lacks the external ID.

[BUG] `deleteEvent` uses the same dead predicate: when `externalCalendarId` is falsy it evaluates `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`, which is always undefined because externalCalendarId is falsy in that branch. Cancelling bookings whose reference lacks externalCalendarId attempts a delete against calendarId undefined, leaving orphaned events on the host's Google Calendar that the previous code (which fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`) would have deleted.

[BUG] `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently no-ops when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null (it is set to null earlier when neither eventType nor organizer has a destination calendar), dropping the collective team members' destination calendars. For a COLLECTIVE event whose organizer/event type has no destination calendar, the team members' calendars are silently never registered — the very 'collective multiple hosts on destinationCalendar' objective of this PR is skipped on the exact path where a null organizer DC is plausible, with no error or log.

[ADVISORY] The `Calendar` interface now mandates `createEvent(event, credentialId: number)`, but only GoogleCalendarService accepts a second parameter; BaseCalendarService, Office365CalendarService, and LarkCalendarService still declare `createEvent(event)`. Every non-Google calendar implementation is now structurally out of contract with the interface it implements; any future caller that relies on the interface (e.g. for per-credential calendar selection, as Google now does) silently gets the old single-DC behavior for O365/Lark/Caldav, diverging per-provider behavior that the next change must rediscover.

[ADVISORY] The booking's persisted `destinationCalendar` relation connects only `evt.destinationCalendar[0].id`, so for COLLECTIVE events with multiple team destination calendars, only the first host's calendar survives on the Booking row. Any later flow reading `booking.destinationCalendar` from the DB (cancellation, reminders, reschedule — all added in this diff) rebuilds the CalendarEvent with a single-element array, so subsequent updates/deletes only see host #1's calendar even though events were created on all hosts' calendars, causing orphaned events on secondary hosts' calendars after cancel/reschedule.

[ADVISORY] `credentialId: result.credentialId ?? undefined` discards the previous fallback to `evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId`, leaving the update-path reference with no credentialId whenever the EventResult lacks one. Bookings whose update result omits credentialId now persist a calendar reference with credentialId undefined, forcing future updates/deletes down the legacy 'iterate all matching credentials' path and calling updateEvent with the wrong credential for multi-credential users.

[BUG] createAllCalendarEvents fetches any credential by destination.credentialId from the database with no ownership/tenant scope check and uses it to create calendar events. A booking whose stored destinationCalendar row contains a credentialId belonging to another user/team is honored: prisma.credential.findUnique({where:{id: destination.credentialId}}) has no userId/teamId filter, so the server instantiates a calendar client with a foreign user's OAuth key and writes events to their calendar — cross-tenant credential use (IDOR), since previously only this.calendarCredentials (scoped to the organizer) were reachable.

[BUG] updateAllCalendarEvents fetches arbitrary credentials from the DB by reference.credentialId with no verification that the credential belongs to the booking's organizer. A booking reference row with a tampered or stale credentialId causes updateEvent to run with another user's calendar credential (including its decrypted key passed to getCalendar), letting one user's stored reference direct writes into any account's calendar; the pre-diff code only selected from the already-scoped this.calendarCredentials list.

[BUG] handleCancelBooking falls back to prisma.credential.findUnique({where:{id: credentialId}}) without filtering by bookingToDelete.user, then uses the returned credential to delete calendar events. If a booking reference's credentialId points at a credential owned by a different user, the cancellation path calls getCalendar with that foreign credential and calendar?.deleteEvent(uid, evt, externalCalendarId) deletes the event from the other user's calendar — unscoped credential lookup turns booking-reference data into cross-account delete capability.

[ADVISORY] The Google event organizer email is replaced with mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId whenever a destinationCalendar exists, without validating that the externalId is an email address owned by the authenticated credential. Any user able to set a destinationCalendar externalId (event-type or user destination calendar) can spoof the organizer identity on Google Calendar event payloads sent under a different host's OAuth credential; combined with the unscoped credential fetch in EventManager, a collective booking can be written to another user's calendar with a forged organizer email.

[ADVISORY] teamDestinationCalendars is populated via a side effect inside the teamMemberPromises map and only for COLLECTIVE events, so a ROUND_ROBIN event's destinationCalendar array stays single-element while the same unscoped credentialId values flow to createAllCalendarEvents. Users booking collective events write events to every host's personal destination calendar, and because those destination rows carry credentialIds consumed without ownership checks (EventManager.ts), the attack surface for cross-user credential use grows with each host added to an event type; behavior also silently differs for ROUND_ROBIN, so event-type misconfiguration determines whose credentials get exercised.

[BUG] The updateEvent fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` can never match, because that branch is only reached when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. When a booking reference has no externalCalendarId, updateEvent now sends calendarId: undefined to the Google API instead of the previous destinationCalendar.externalId, so reschedule/editLocation updates of pre-refactor bookings fail or hit the wrong calendar.

[BUG] deleteEvent has the same dead fallback: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is evaluated only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so find always misses and calendarId is undefined. Cancelling a booking whose reference lacks externalCalendarId now calls calendar.events.delete with calendarId: undefined; Google returns 4xx and the event is never removed from the host's calendar even though the booking is cancelled.

[BUG] `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op when destinationCalendar is null (organizer has no destinationCalendar and eventType has none), silently dropping the collected team destination calendars. A COLLECTIVE team event whose organizer lacks a destinationCalendar creates calendar events only via the default credential path while every teammate's destinationCalendar is discarded, so hosts' calendars miss the booking with no error surfaced.

[BUG] createEvent sets the organizer attendee email from `mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` (always the FIRST destinationCalendar) while the target calendar is selected per credentialId, so for the second and later hosts the organizer email belongs to a different host's calendar. For a collective booking with two Google hosts, the event created on host B's calendar carries host A's destination email as organizer; Google rejects or misattributes the organizer, producing broken events on non-primary hosts.

[ADVISORY] The diff's only test change is updating a fixture literal from `destinationCalendar: null` to `[]` in the BOOKING_REJECTED snapshot; no test anywhere in the diff asserts the new array semantics (per-credential calendar selection in GoogleCalendarService, the EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents multi-destination loop, the DB credential-fetch fallback, or the collective teamDestinationCalendars push). The webhook.e2e.ts snapshot passes identically whether the multi-host selection logic is correct or not (it asserts a static payload for a rejected booking that never reaches calendar creation), so the PR's headline behavior — collective events landing on every host's calendar — ships with zero verification; the first regression will be silent wrong-calendar writes discovered by users.

[BUG] The fallback branch of selectedCalendar in updateEvent is a dead lookup that can never match, and the same defect is duplicated in deleteEvent (lines 312-315). When externalCalendarId is null/empty (bookings whose BookingReference stored no externalCalendarId), the code executes event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId, where externalCalendarId is falsy so the find never matches and the expression is always undefined; calendarId becomes undefined and the Google events.update/events.delete call targets no calendar, so reschedules and cancellations of pre-existing bookings fail against Google's API and the remote event is left orphaned on the user's calendar — a regression from the old behavior which fell back to event.destinationCalendar?.externalId.

[BUG] The DB persists only the first destination calendar (connect of evt.destinationCalendar[0]) while EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents creates real events on every COLLECTIVE host's calendar, so references to the additional hosts' events are never written to the database. For a COLLECTIVE booking with multiple hosts, createAllCalendarEvents (EventManager.ts:341-380) creates one calendar event per entry in evt.destinationCalendar, but the prisma.booking.create destinationCalendar connect uses only evt.destinationCalendar[0]; because there is no migration or schema change in this diff, Booking.destinationCalendar remains a single relation, so the other hosts' BookingReferences are never recorded (the results array is consumed only for references on the merged evt). Any later cancel or reschedule resolves the calendar from bookingToDelete.destinationCalendar (handleCancelBooking.ts:248-254) which is only the first host's calendar — the events created on the other hosts' calendars can never be updated or deleted and remain orphaned on their Google/Office365 calendars.

[BUG] In the reschedule path, when the reference's credentialId matches no calendarCredential in this.calendarCredentials and the prisma.credential.findUnique returns null, the local variable credential stays undefined and updateEvent(credential, event, ...) is still called with undefined. updateEvent(undefined, ...) dereferences credential.id / getCalendar(undefined) and throws a TypeError (prisma 'Malformed ObjectID' or getCalendar crash), so a reschedule of a booking whose referenced credential was deleted or belongs to a different user crashes instead of returning the graceful failure result the catch block promises — the booking update request fails with a 500.

[ADVISORY] The reschedule cancellation email drops the previous fallback chain entirely: the old code (already buggy with a duplicated expression) never fell back to the user's destinationCalendar, and the new code likewise ignores user.destinationCalendar, sending an empty array when the booking has none. Organizers whose bookings lack a booking-level destinationCalendar (relying on their user-level destinationCalendar) receive cancellation emails whose BrokenIntegrationEmail/calendar rendering takes the 'calendar' default branch instead of naming their connected calendar; users get a degraded but non-crashing email, only in the requestReschedule flow.

[BUG] createEvent now unconditionally returns the caller-supplied externalId as result.externalId, but in the EventManager no-credentialId branch createEvent(c, event) is invoked without the third argument, so the created booking reference stores externalCalendarId undefined while the event was actually created on a calendar selected inside the provider. For destination calendars without credentialId (legacy path, EventManager.ts:370-375), EventManager writes externalCalendarId: result.externalId === undefined into the BookingReference; on later update/delete, GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent/deleteEvent hit the dead fallback (finding 1) or pass calendarId undefined, so those events can never be moved or removed — remote calendar data is silently orphaned on reschedule/cancel.

[BUG] In updateEvent, when externalCalendarId is falsy the selectedCalendar is computed as `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`, which searches for an externalId equal to a falsy value and can never match, so selectedCalendar is always undefined and the update is sent with calendarId undefined. For bookings whose stored reference has no externalCalendarId (all pre-refactor bookings, and the fallback path where CalendarManager returns externalId undefined), calendar.events.update receives no calendarId, Google rejects the call, and rescheduling/edits of existing bookings fail with a Google API error where the old code resolved the calendar from destinationCalendar.externalId.

[BUG] In deleteEvent, the fallback branch is `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`, so when externalCalendarId is absent the find predicate compares against the absent value and always yields undefined. Deleting a booking whose calendar reference lacks externalCalendarId calls calendar.events.delete with calendarId undefined, Google throws 'Missing required query parameter: calendarId', and the calendar event is left on the user's Google Calendar while the booking is reported as cancelled — a silently dangling event.

[BUG] `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` no-ops when evt.destinationCalendar is null (which it is whenever eventType.destinationCalendar and organizerUser.destinationCalendar are both unset), silently dropping all team members' destination calendars for a COLLECTIVE event. A collective booking whose event type and organizer have no destination calendar configured will not be created on any team member's calendar, and no error or warning is surfaced — the API reports full success while the multi-host calendar sync is silently skipped.

[BUG] createEvent falls back to `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"` when no destinationCalendar entry matches the given credentialId, creating the event on the account's primary calendar with no warning or error. A collective booking where a member's destinationCalendar references a credential that was deleted or belongs to another app gets its event silently written to that member's primary Google calendar instead of the intended one; the operation reports success and the booking reference records the wrong externalCalendarId, so later updates/deletes target the wrong calendar.

[ADVISORY] createEvent (and updateEvent at ~line 227) always uses the first destinationCalendar's externalId as the organizer email, even when the event is being created on a different host's calendar selected via credentialId. For collective events with multiple Google hosts, the event created on the second host's calendar carries the first host's destination-calendar email as organizer; Google rejects or mangles events where the organizer does not belong to the target calendar, and attendees see the wrong organizer on secondary hosts' copies.

[BUG] loadUsers throws a generic 500 ('Unable to load users') for entirely user-controllable conditions — empty dynamicUserList on a dynamic group link and a non-array eventType.hosts — instead of a 4xx. A booker hitting a dynamic link whose user list resolves to empty (e.g. all hosts removed from the URL) gets a 500 Internal Server Error from the booking API rather than a 400/404, breaking the error contract and making client-side handling (which distinguishes 'no valid users' from server failure) impossible.

[ADVISORY] In updateEvent, when the reference's credentialId is not in this.calendarCredentials and the DB lookup returns nothing, `updateEvent(credential, ...)` is still called with credential undefined, unlike createAllCalendarEvents which guards with `if (credential)`. The undefined credential reaches CalendarManager's getCalendar/credential destructuring and throws a TypeError; the surrounding catch then returns success:false for every calendar reference, so one stale/missing credential (e.g. a deleted teammate credential on a collective booking) marks all calendar updates as failed instead of skipping the one dead reference.

[ADVISORY] createEvent returns `externalId` unconditionally from the caller-supplied parameter, but the fallback path in EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents calls createEvent without the third argument, so those results carry externalId undefined where the previous code populated externalCalendarId from evt.destinationCalendar.externalId. Bookings created via the match-all-credentials fallback path store calendar references with a null externalCalendarId, which then route into the broken falsy-externalCalendarId branches of GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent/deleteEvent and fail on every subsequent reschedule or cancellation.

goldens.comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
